mtle.Description: Binary variable indicating if spontaneous seizures originated from mesial-temporal structures (mesial temporal lobe epilepsy)

unifocal.Description: Binary yes/no describing whether clinical impression based on recorded spontaneous seizures was of a single focal epileptogenic zone (Yes) or distributed network (No)

Levels.No: distributed network (diffuse or multiple focal onset zones)

lesional.Description: Indicates whether epileptogenic abnormalities were detected on pre-surgical imaging

outcome.Description: Most recent available Engel score for post-surgical seizure outcome. Decimal values denote Engel subclasses (e.g., 1.1 = Engel IA, 1.2 = Engel IB). Patients treated with an implanted neurostimulation device rather than resective/ablative surgery are coded Device. Missing values are coded n/a. Integer part (Engel class): 1 = Engel I: free of disabling seizures; 2 = Engel II: rare disabling seizures; 3 = Engel III: worthwhile improvement; 4 = Engel IV: no worthwhile improvement; Device = treated with an implanted neurostimulation device; n/a = outcome data unavailable.

follow_up.Description: Time after surgery at which the most recent available Engel score was assessed

n_seizures.Description: Number of seizures included from that patient

n_stim_induced.Description: Number of seizures that were induced with low-frequency stimulation

diagnosis.Description: epilepsy (all subjects; drug-resistant epilepsy undergoing SEEG)

implant_type.Description: sEEG (all channels typed SEEG in channels.tsv / SEEGChannelCount in _ieeg.json)

site.Description: Center inferred from subject code prefix as described in annotations.json ("adult (HUP) or pediatric (CHOP) center")

n_contacts.Description: Number of rows (contacts) in the subject derivatives/electrodes.tsv

implanted_hemisphere.Description: Hemisphere(s) of the contacts per the DK brain_area labels (Left-/Right-/ctx-lh-/ctx-rh-) of electrodes.tsv; derived by counting, not stated by the authors

soz_contacts.Description: Union over the subject's seizures of the consensus unequivocal-electrographic-onset channels (majority vote of 3-5 clinicians)
